title: Unpublished Results Show NMNH Triples NAD+ in First Human Trial
abstract: # Unpublished Results Show NMNH Triples NAD+ in First Human Trial. According to newly released results from a first-of-its-kind clinical trial, reduced nicotinamide mononucleotide (NMNH) triples circulating NAD+ and improves subjective quality of life scores. As for what the unpublished and non-peer-reviewed results of the trial say, Morgan reported that NMNH approximately tripled circulating levels of NAD+ in a dose-dependent manner. However, the interpretation of the SF-36 scores for the NMNH human trial for comparison is tricky, because the results were reported as percentages. As such, the way the SF-36 scores were reported in the NMNH human trial makes judging the clinical magnitude of NMNH’s effects on energy levels and emotional well-being very difficult. Collectively, the data from the first NMNH human trial suggest that NMNH appears to raise NAD+ in humans significantly, is well-tolerated over 90 days, and participants who took NMNH report improvements in subjective energy and mood.
